topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture themes on cancer evolution and outlines the session's key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal selection and tumor initiation.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the cancer stem cell hypothesis and review experimental evidence regarding how cell hierarchy and the cell of origin influence tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how external promoters, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stromal cells create permissive conditions for tumor outgrowth and therapeutic intervention.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental, genomic, and computational tools used to map tumor heterogeneity, cellular interactions, and evolutionary timing.

topics.label: Integrated model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the combined roles of mutational burden, cell-of-origin properties, and microenvironmental pressures into a unified evolutionary framework of cancer progression.

topics.label: Closing remarks and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
